steps.title: Terraces by the sea
steps.body: Bandol lies on the Mediterranean coast of Provence, between Marseille and Toulon. Vineyards climb an amphitheatre of terraces, called restanques, facing south to the sea. Hot, sunny days and sea breezes ripen Mourvèdre fully. Limestone and sandy marl soils keep the vines healthy.

steps.title: Rules
steps.body: Bandol red must be at least 50% Mourvèdre, with Grenache and Cinsault, and age at least 18 months in oak before release. Most top producers use 75 to 95% Mourvèdre. The wines are dark, structured, gamey and herbal, and can age 20 years or more.
steps.highlight: At least 50% Mourvèdre, 18 months in oak

steps.prompt: Bandol red must age at least ____ months in oak.
steps.explanation: Eighteen months in wood softens Mourvèdre's firm tannins.

steps.title: Rosé and white
steps.body: Bandol's rosé is among Provence's most serious: more structured than most, often with Mourvèdre at its core, and able to age a few years. The small amount of white wine uses Clairette, Ugni Blanc and Bourboulenc. Domaine Tempier, a family estate, helped define Bandol's modern reputation.

steps.prompt: Bandol rosé is often more structured than typical Provence rosé.
steps.explanation: Yes. Mourvèdre gives it more body and ageing potential.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Bandol's terraces face the sea, ripening Mourvèdre fully
Reds need at least 50% Mourvèdre and 18 months in oak
Bandol rosé is structured and can age
